Subject: Billing mechanics questions before SOW sign

Michael —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at StellarChain is reviewing the SOW and we have a couple of billing mechanics items we need clarified before the legal/finance teams will sign:

1) Minimums & rounding: the SOW references a 100k token monthly minimum for the pilot. How do you apply rounding for short-lived requests (e.g., a 50-token call)? Do you round up per-call, per-session, or do you accumulate across the month and apply a single rounding rule at invoice time? We need to understand invoice behavior for small, frequent calls.

2) Long context windows: Our assistant will routinely send combined documents ~18k tokens. How does Redwood account for context length vs model tokenization? Is there a distinct bucket for >16k contexts, or do you split and bill as multiple calls? We want an example invoice row to show our finance team.

3) Quantized/CPU fallback: you mentioned cheaper quantized variants and occasional CPU fallback for capacity. If a request is served by a quantized variant or falls back to CPU, is billing different or do you charge by logical tokens regardless of execution path?

4) Escrowed credits: For pilots, we're asking vendors to accept an escrowed credit that can be consumed for overages. Is Redwood able to accept and consume escrow credits from a third-party payment, and how are credits applied against rounding/minimums?

Would appreciate a short worked example and any sample invoice rows (CSV is fine). Attached our internal procurement checklist for context.

Best,
Alex Park
Head of Platform Partnerships
StellarChain

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Billing mechanics questions before SOW sign

Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. I put together a concise answer + a small sample CSV (attached) that maps the scenarios you asked about to invoice rows. High level answers first, then the CSV example:

1) Minimums & rounding — We use monthly aggregation with a per-call minimum of 1 billing unit (a billing unit = 10 logical tokens for the selected SKU) and then apply an invoice-level rounding rule at month end. Practically that means: short calls can be accumulated in the same month and are NOT rounded up individually at the invoice line level. We floor per-call to the unit granularity, sum all units in a calendar month, then round the final subtotal to the nearest billing quantum defined in the contract.

2) Long contexts (>16k) — For requests that exceed the supported per-call context, we stitch server-side and count tokens across the logical request. If stitching requires splitting into multiple model calls, we still produce a single invoice row that attributes the total logical prompt+completion tokens to that user request, plus an internal flag showing it was served as N calls. In short: you get a single logical accounting line. We'll show both the logical token count and the call-level breakdown in the CSV.

3) Quantized/CPU fallback — Billing is by logical tokens and the SKU you agreed to in the SOW. Execution path (quantized variant, CPU fallback) does not change customer-facing billing. We include internal notes about cheaper kernel execution for capacity planning, but the price to you is stable per the SKU unless you opt in to a special discounted quantized SKU.

4) Escrowed credits — We can accept third-party escrowed credits if your procurement/legal team provides an invoicing flow and verifies the payment method. Credits are applied at invoice settlement and will reduce the invoice subtotal after rounding is applied (i.e., rounding happens, line items totaled, then credits and concessions applied). For the pilot concession you're proposing, we can honor an escrowed $15k credit that Redwood will apply monthly until exhausted.

I attached: StellarChain_SOW_v2.pdf (annotated SOW with the billing clause highlighted) and a billing_sample.csv showing three sample invoice rows: small frequent calls aggregated, a stitched 18k-context request, and a monthly summary with the escrow credit applied.

Next steps: happy to jump on a 30-min call with procurement/legal to walk the invoice sample. If acceptable, we can add an explicit "escrow credit" clause to the SOW and a HubSpot comment pointing to the DocuSign envelope.

Cheers,
Michael Grant
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: StellarChain_SOW_v2.pdf (PDF); billing_sample.csv (CSV)]
